title: Dependency correlation playbook & observability pipeline for cross-team roadmaps
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: As we scale Dedicated and Private deployments, roadmap delivery increasingly depends on cross-team sequencing (Serving runtime, Console UX, Security sign-offs, infra capacity). We lack a single, actionable signal that correlates open work across Eng/Design/Security/Infra into a prioritized dependency list and automated escalation path.

Goal: Build a lightweight dependency telemetry and escalation pipeline + an accompanying playbook so PMs and engineering managers can: (1) see correlated dependencies on roadmap items, (2) get proactive alerts when dependencies threaten a milestone, and (3) run a clear escalation workflow that reduces manual coordination overhead.

Scope: This ticket covers the definition of correlation signals, the initial observability dashboard (Console + weekly digest), the priority scoring model, and the escalation playbook. Implementation tasks will be split across Eng (ingestion + scoring service), PM (playbook + owner mapping), Design (dashboard UX), and Security (access controls for ingestion).
acceptance_criteria: A dependency scoring prototype that consumes Linear + GitHub cross-references + release tags and outputs a priority score for each dependent issue (score 0-100)
A Console dashboard mock and an initial working dashboard that shows top 50 dependency correlations across projects, filterable by team and release
A documented escalation playbook with thresholds, contact methods (Slack/Email), and owner handoff steps
Weekly automated digest emailed to designated owners with top 10 high-risk dependencies
Security review completed for ingestion pipeline and access to dependency data (audit log present)
tasks: PM: Define correlation signals and thresholds (labels, blocking links, PR blockers, release mismatch, due_date proximity)
ENG: Build a lightweight ingestion lambda to pull Linear issues, GitHub PR references, and release tags (initial cadence: hourly)
ENG: Implement scoring service with configurable weights and persistence (runtime DB)
DES: Design dashboard mockups and weekly digest email template; define filters and table columns
SEC: Review data ingestion permissions; add audit logging and RBAC constraints
PM/EM: Run two pilot weeks with roadmap owners and collect feedback
PM: Draft escalation playbook (triggers, Slack routing, templates, exec-brief cadence)
notes_and_updates: 2025-02-07 - Maya Chen: Kickoff. Identified high-value signals: 'blocks', 'linked PRs with failing checks', release tag mismatch, and unassigned critical owner. Prioritize an initial MVP that avoids heavy instrumentation.
2025-02-10 - Anika Sharma: Shared sample dataset (40 roadmap items) across infra/serving/console for scoring experiments. Agreed to start with hourly ingestion and adjustable weight config.
2025-02-13 - Ravi Patel (ENG): Prototype ingestion lambda working against a staging Linear export. Found noisy links from archived tickets; added rule to ignore issues closed > 90 days ago.

2025-02-17 - Design review: Dashboard table should include fields: dependent_issue, dependency(s), score, due_date, owner, teams_involved, last_activity. Added quick-actions: 'ping owner' and 'open escalation'.
2025-02-20 - Security review kickoff: SEC requested encrypted storage for cross-references and a per-team access control list. Marked security_review_required = true and added SEC-42 as a dependency.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP, 3 weeks): build ingestion + scoring config and a staging dashboard; trial with 2 product teams. Phase 2 (4 weeks): add weekly digest, escalation automation (Slack), and security hardening. Phase 3 (Q2): refine scoring weights from feedback, publish runbook org-wide and onboard remaining teams.
open_questions: What exact threshold should trigger an automatic escalation to PG+EMs vs. remains as a PM alert (suggested scoring thresholds: 70/90)
How do we represent transitive dependencies (A depends on B depends on C) in the UI without overwhelming owners?
Do we store historical trend of dependency scores for regressions/OKR retrospective analysis?
